title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on Legally and Effectively Ensuring Lawyers' Litigation Rights
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on Ensuring Lawyers' Litigation Rights in Accordance with Law

Fa Fa [2015] No. 16

High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Provisions on Ensuring Lawyers' Litigation Rights in Accordance with Law formulated by the Supreme People's Court are hereby issued for your earnest implementation.

December 29, 2015

Provisions on Ensuring Lawyers' Litigation Rights in Accordance with Law

For the purpose of thoroughly implementing the strategy of comprehensively advancing the rule of law, giving full play to the positive role of lawyers in safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of the parties and promoting judicial fairness, and effectively ensuring lawyers' litigation rights, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law, the Civil Procedure Law, the Administrative Procedure Law, and the Lawyers Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Provisions on Ensuring Lawyers' Practice Rights in Accordance with Law jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice.

I. Ensure lawyers' right to be informed in accordance with law. People's courts shall continuously improve the construction of the "three major platforms" for the disclosure of trial procedures, judgment documents, and enforcement information, to facilitate lawyers' timely access to litigation information. For important matters such as litigation procedures, protection of litigation rights, mediation and settlement, and judgment documents, as well as related progress, lawyers shall be informed in a timely manner in accordance with law.

II. Ensure lawyers' right to review case files in accordance with law. Where a lawyer applies to review case files, arrangements shall be made within a reasonable time. Where case file materials have been reviewed by other litigation participants, the court shall coordinate the arrangement of review times for all parties. Where a lawyer reviews, extracts, or copies relevant case file materials or views court hearing audio or video recordings in accordance with law, premises and facilities shall be provided. Courts with the conditions may provide online case file review services.

III. Ensure lawyers' right to appear in court in accordance with law. When determining the trial date, necessary preparation time for appearance in court shall be reserved for lawyers. If the trial date is changed due to special circumstances, lawyers shall be notified three days in advance. Where a lawyer requests a change of trial date on legitimate grounds, the judge may grant the request after consulting the opinions of other parties. Where a lawyer brings an assistant to appear in court, this shall be permitted.

IV. Ensure lawyers' right to debate and defend in accordance with law. During court proceedings, judges shall reasonably allocate time for the parties to ask questions, examine evidence, make statements, debate, and defend, and shall fully hear lawyers' opinions. Except where the lawyer's statements are excessively repetitive, irrelevant to the case, or the relevant issues have been agreed upon prior to trial, the lawyer's statements shall not be interrupted.

V. Ensure lawyers' right to apply for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence in accordance with law. Where a lawyer applies for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and provides relevant clues or materials, and the judge has doubts about the legality of the evidence collection after review, a pre-trial conference shall be held or a court investigation shall be conducted. If it is confirmed after review that evidence was collected by illegal methods as provided by law, the relevant evidence shall be excluded.

VI. Ensure lawyers' right to apply for the collection of evidence in accordance with law. Where a lawyer cannot collect evidence on his/her own due to objective reasons, he/she may apply to the people's court in writing for the collection of evidence in accordance with law. Where the lawyer's application for collection of evidence meets the statutory conditions, the judge shall grant it.

VII. Ensure lawyers' personal safety in accordance with law. Where, during the trial of a case, conflicts between the parties escalate and may endanger the lawyer's personal safety, necessary measures shall be taken promptly. Where acts such as assault, threats, insults, or defamation against lawyers occur in the courtroom, the judge shall promptly stop them and handle them in accordance with law.

VIII. Ensure lawyers' right to represent petitions in accordance with law. Where a lawyer represents a party in filing a petition regarding a case, the court shall handle it seriously in accordance with the procedures provided by law. If the court considers that the original case was correctly handled, the court shall support the lawyer in explaining the law and reasoning to the petitioner to facilitate the dropping of the petition and the ending of the case.

IX. Provide convenience for lawyers to perform their duties in accordance with law. The court shall further improve functions such as online case filing, payment of fees, inquiries, review of case files, application for preservation, submission of legal arguments, scheduling of court sessions, and service of documents. Courts with the conditions shall provide rest areas, tables, chairs, drinking water, and other necessary facilities for lawyers attending court sessions.

X. Improve the relief mechanism for ensuring lawyers' litigation rights. A specialized office shall be designated to handle lawyers' complaints, with publicly available contact information and unimpeded complaint channels. Complaints shall be investigated promptly, handled in accordance with law, and the results shall be promptly notified to the lawyer. Suggestions raised by judicial administrative organs and bar associations regarding the protection of lawyers' practice rights shall be responded to promptly.
